final_label: D1 right after a reward that came from choosing a2 and reaching S2 via the common transition, while the observed history favours S2 (belief < 0.4), before episode trial 78

with_model_outputs.label: D1 after a reward, when the agent is about to choose a2 (episode trials < ~78)
with_model_outputs.explanation: Fires only at D1 (never GO or D2), and essentially only when the reward input is 1 (previous trial rewarded) and the policy logit already favours a2 (choice < -1.52; all activation mass is in the [-4.44,-1.52] choice bin), i.e. the agent is set to stay with a2 after a reward (prev_action is 2 and the previous transition common in ~all non-first trials). The upcoming choice is the agents own computation and no unobservable future outcome is used; the version using the future variable action==2 instead of the choice logit is clearly worse (F1 0.71, or 0.82 with the episode cutoff). It is silent after unrewarded trials, before a1 choices, and late in episodes (almost no activity from episode trial ~80 on; adding ep_trial < 78 raises dev F1 from 0.79 to 0.90). Activation is concentrated at mid-range value (7.1-7.7). Magnitude often sits near max (~1.0) on runs of rewarded a2 trials, with weaker (0.3-0.7) activations in some windows; I did not pin down the magnitude modulator. Dev: P 0.85, R 0.96, F1 0.90, mass recall 0.997.

issues: Systematic false-positive class: the feature is silent at D1 after a rewarded RARE transition, even when choice < -1.52 and ep_trial < 78. Adding (prev_common == 0) to the original predicate gives 6928 predicted dev steps at precision 0.014. That is about 57% of the 12208 dev false positives.

So the label 'D1 after a reward, when the agent is about to choose a2' overclaims. The feature needs the previous trial to be a common (or unknown, at the start of the window) rewarded a2 trial. The explanation notes that active cases mostly follow common transitions, but it presents this as incidental. In fact a rare-rewarded previous trial is an exclusion: the feature is off there despite reward == 1 and an a2-leaning logit.
The low rel +1 precision (0.57, against about 0.90 for the other rels) comes mostly from this same rare-prev class. With prev_common != 0 added, rel +1 precision rises to 0.94.
Adding (prev_common != 0) to the predicate raises test precision from 0.845 to 0.928 at the same recall (0.956). Test F1 goes from 0.898 to 0.942.

The other claims check out. The feature has zero activity at GO and D2. There are essentially no activations with in_rew == 0 or with the choice logit favouring a1. Almost no activity from trial 80 on. Without the ep_trial cutoff, test F1 drops to 0.83.
The observed-only stand-in for the choice logit (prev_action != 1) is much worse: test F1 0.77. So the upcoming-choice term is doing real work, and it is legitimate (the agent's own computation).
skeptic.revised_label: D1 after a common-transition rewarded trial (not rare-rewarded) when the agent is about to choose a2, i.e. the model-based 'stay with a2' signal; episode trials < ~78

with_model_outputs.final_label: D1 after a common-transition rewarded trial (not rare-rewarded) when the agent is about to choose a2, i.e. the model-based 'stay with a2' signal; episode trials < ~78

label: D1 right after a reward that came from choosing a2 and reaching S2 via the common transition, while the observed history favours S2 (belief < 0.4), before episode trial 78
explanation: Fires only at D1, and only when the reward input is 1. The rewarded previous trial must have been a2 with a common transition (a2 to S2). After a1 or a rare transition it almost never fires. Belief < 0.4 (the ideal observer thinks S2 is likely good) covers window-start steps that have no previous trial, and it removes some cases where the history is mixed. The feature is silent from about episode trial 78 on. Remaining false positives are mostly a2-common rewards that follow an unrewarded or rare trial. Requiring the trial before to be rewarded raises precision to 0.91 but lowers recall to 0.81. Magnitude was not checked.

issues: Claims check out on test: D1-only (all activation mass at D1); after a1 (prev_action==1) precision 0.0001 and after rare (prev_common==0) precision 0.004, so 'almost never' holds; ep_trial>=78 slice has precision 0.05 / recall 0.017, so the late-episode silence is real.

Adding the model's upcoming choice (action==2) barely helps (F1 0.855 -> 0.858), even though nearly all activation falls on steps followed by an a2 choice; the observed rule is not missing a choice-driven component.

Stated FP class confirmed: when the trial two back was unrewarded, precision drops to 0.46 (12.7k predicted). Excluding it costs recall; the best tweak tried (~((tv('reward',-2)==0)&(belief>0.2))) only gives test F1 0.860.

Minor: window-start D1 steps with belief>=0.4 are missed (about 4% of recall); the lowest activation quartile is covered only 0.81; the ep_trial<78 cutoff is a fitted empirical boundary (70-77 still fires at precision 0.63).
